nodes.label: BatchSizer (~250 ms GPU submissions)
nodes.rationale: Fixed 16-dispatch batches left the GPU at ~70% because host readback and CPU checks ran between small batches; sizing batches to ~250 ms raised load to 95-100%.

nodes.label: Profile LoadVersion
nodes.rationale: The tuning score changed with the new load, so profiles record LoadVersion and auto-overclock never reuses a stock measurement from the old load.

nodes.label: App self-update (from 0.7.0)
nodes.rationale: Files replaced in place, Data untouched, previous files kept in Data\cache\update\previous and restored on failure; log in Data\logs\update.log.

nodes.label: Two editions: Mazesta (Admin) and Client
nodes.rationale: Published update is the Client edition, so the Mazesta edition never self-installs it (it would turn into the Client edition).

nodes.label: UPDATES.md (app self-update, site plugin, benchmark lists)
nodes.norm_label: updates.md (app self-update, site plugin, benchmark lists)

nodes.label: Benchmark mode (reduced sensor polling)
nodes.rationale: While a benchmark runs: no live page data or animations, only CPU/GPU/RAM plus overlay sensors read, tray checks and update checks postponed, to avoid disturbing the measurement.

nodes.label: Benchmark runs log (Data\benchmarks\runs\*.jsonl, marks.json)
nodes.rationale: Unreadable values are not recorded (no guessing); GPU core count omitted as no reliable Windows source.

nodes.label: Update-signing private key (mazesta-update-private.pem)
nodes.rationale: If lost, installed copies accept no further updates; keep two backups, never in git or on the site. A hacked site cannot push code because the app verifies signature plus size and SHA-256.

nodes.label: update.json signed manifest
nodes.rationale: Upload update.json and .sig last so a client checking mid-upload never asks for a file not yet there; format numbered (format: 1) so old clients ignore unknown formats.

nodes.label: Separate CRM database (mz_* tables)
nodes.rationale: CRM kept apart from WordPress DB; password encrypted with wp-config keys. HTML reports, benchmark data and stats stay files (large, built once); link via report_id is enough until tens of thousands of reports.

nodes.label: Customer portal [mazesta_portal]
nodes.rationale: Unknown numbers get the same response and no SMS, to avoid revealing who is a customer.

nodes.label: Mazesta Connect WordPress plugin
nodes.rationale: All app-to-site traffic goes through one plugin under /wp-json/mazesta/v1/; legacy bridge data kept in files (mazesta-connect-data) not WordPress DB since 1.1.0; backup = that folder.

nodes.label: Old CRM import (export_old_crm.py, old-crm.jsonl.gz)
nodes.rationale: Stepwise import, idempotent, customers merged by mobile; file holds customer data so never commit it.

nodes.label: Stock / products (Connect 2.5.0)
nodes.rationale: Stock is never entered by hand: purchases minus parts used in builds and jobs, so deleting a wrong invoice or part self-corrects.

nodes.label: Messages to installed systems
nodes.rationale: Polled every 8h (max 3/day), keyless with random install id, only when anonymous stats is on.

nodes.label: MazestaDesk.exe (staff program)
nodes.rationale: All site calls go through C# (only /staff/ paths, https only); token sealed with DPAPI in Data\desk.json and never reaches the page.

nodes.label: MCP server for ChatGPT / Claude
nodes.rationale: Each MCP tool is the staff API under the same person's session: same access and audit log; AI never sees the password; disabling account or changing password cuts the link.

nodes.label: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE and dynamic registration
nodes.norm_label: oauth 2.1 with pkce and dynamic registration

nodes.label: Pairing by site sign-in (pair/start, pair/claim)
nodes.rationale: App keeps a random secret and sends only its SHA-256; admin confirms the six-letter code; key fetched once.

nodes.label: Automatic service number R-n
nodes.rationale: Database lock so two people never get the same number; new computers (2.5.0) use invoice number instead.

nodes.label: BenchmarkRecords.Headlines version
nodes.rationale: Raise the version when a workload changes so incomparable results are never compared.

nodes.label: Benchmark comparison lists (benchdb)
nodes.rationale: One list per benchmark x workload version x settings; one row per part model (median of each system's best run) so size grows with models not runs; each system counted once; median neutralises outliers.

nodes.label: Benchmark privacy (no computer name in lists)
nodes.norm_label: benchmark privacy (no computer name in lists)
